title: How can a customer buy more free time on a running container record?
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category governs the purchase of a higher free-time product for a per-container record while its free time is still running, the price charged for it, and its effect on the record.

## Policy clauses

1. While a record's free time is still running, the billed party may buy a higher product for it.
2. A product can be bought only while the record's status is free time running; once charges accrue it is too late, and the purchase is never backdated.
3. The product bought must be purchasable as an upgrade, must have a higher rank than the product on the record, and the container's rate class must be one of its eligible rate classes. AHL Contract Free Time 30 is never sold.
4. A record may take an upgrade only while the number of upgrades already bought on it is below the number of upgrades the product currently on it still allows. The upgrades counted are every extension fee charged on the record over its life.
5. The price charged is the list price of the product bought less the list price of the product already on the record, so the customer never pays twice for the same days. The price is charged to the record as an extension fee.
6. The upgrade replaces the product on the record and, under the clock rules, governs every clock of the record.
7. Purchases are also subject to the rule on the customer's overdue demurrage and detention balance.
8. A bought product is not refundable when the container is returned early.

## Evidence

The record's status and its history of extension fees are read from the line's records before the purchase.

## Eligibility checklist

| Check | Must hold |
|---|---|
| Record status | free time running |
| Product bought | purchasable as an upgrade, and not AHL Contract Free Time 30 |
| Rank | higher than the product on the record |
| Container rate class | one of the eligible rate classes of the product bought |
| Upgrades already bought on the record | fewer than the product currently on the record allows |

## Worked cases (hypothetical list prices and allowances, chosen only for illustration)

- A record carries a product with an illustrative list price of USD 100.00 and the customer buys one listed at USD 300.00: the extension fee is USD 300.00 less USD 100.00, that is USD 200.00.
- The product on a record allows an illustrative 1 upgrade and no extension fee has yet been charged on the record: an upgrade may be taken. Once one extension fee has been charged, the count is no longer below 1 and no further upgrade may be taken while that allowance applies.
- A clock passed its free days yesterday and the record now shows charges accruing: the purchase is too late and cannot be dated back to yesterday.

## Points of judgement

**Q: The container came back early after an upgrade. Is the upgrade price returned?**
A: No. A bought product is not refundable when the container is returned early.
